decision_conditions:
This is notice that on the 20th of October, the council made the following order TP26/0018

Copies of this order will be delivered to the relevant addresses. In summary it prohibits anyone from cutting down, topping or lopping any of the trees described, without the Council's Consent.

The Council has made the Order on the following grounds:
A Section 211 Notification was recently received (ref: PA26/3300) proposing the removal of a Magnolia situated within the front garden of 9 Beverley Road. The justification provided states that the tree is considered too large for its location and alleges that roots may be contributing to damage to the property and surrounding hardstanding.

The Magnolia occupies a prominent position within the frontage of the property and is readily visible from Beverley Road. The tree is a prominent landscape feature within the street scene, making a positive contribution to the character and appearance of the local area through its size, form and year round green softening.

Whilst concerns have been raised regarding alleged damage associated with the tree, no supporting arboricultural, engineering, structural or other technical evidence has been submitted to substantiate these claims or demonstrate that removal of the tree is necessary. As such, the information provided is insufficient to justify the loss of a tree that makes a significant contribution to public amenity. The loss of the tree would be readily apparent from the public realm and would result in a noticeable reduction in local amenity, and it is considered expedient in the interest of amenity to safeguard the tree with this tree preservation order.
